content: The document outlines a systematic review and subsequent updates regarding the use of micronutrient powders (MNPs) for point-of-use food fortification in children. The review, initially published in 2011 and updated in October 2016, is undergoing editorial processing with the Cochrane Developmental, Psychosocial, and Learning Problems Group. Cochrane reviews are regularly updated to incorporate new evidence and feedback, and the latest version can be accessed in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. The systematic review evaluates the effects and safety of using MNPs containing iron in children aged 6–23 months and 2–12 years. Key questions addressed include whether MNPs improve health outcomes, and if so, the optimal dose, frequency, and duration of use. The review also examines the impact of MNPs on anemia, iron status, hemoglobin levels, and, in malaria-endemic areas, malaria incidence and severity. Comparisons are made against no intervention, placebo, or iron supplements. The evidence quality was rated as moderate for anemia, low for hemoglobin, and very low for iron status (ferritin concentrations). The World Health Organization (WHO) guideline development group considered the intervention generally acceptable to healthcare providers and families. However, one-third of the group believed the benefits and harms were balanced, while three-quarters felt the benefits justified the costs. The feasibility of implementation was deemed conditional on specific settings and anemia prevalence, with 63% of the group finding it feasible in certain contexts. The group emphasized that MNPs are not the sole policy option for increasing iron intake, and decision-makers should tailor interventions to their specific needs and resources. The guideline development process involved contributions from experts in nutrition, public health, and related fields, as well as peer reviewers. The names and affiliations of contributors and reviewers are acknowledged, though their inclusion does not imply endorsement of the recommendations.
